reason: E1 demonstrates transformation toughening by in-situ ZrO2 in a high-entropy carbide, supporting the mechanism and toughness enhancement, but it is a ceramic, not a metallic caloric alloy. E2 concerns SiC reinforcement in a high-entropy alloy composite and does not address ZrO2, transformation toughening, or caloric properties. The key premise that caloric performance is preserved is entirely unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: In-situ metastable tetragonal ZrO2 particles can be precipitated in a high-entropy alloy matrix by adding Zr and controlled heat treatment
These ZrO2 particles undergo a stress-induced tetragonal-to-monoclinic transformation that triggers crack-tip shielding mechanisms (deflection, bridging, branching)
This transformation toughening significantly enhances fracture toughness in high-entropy systems
The toughening mechanism does not substantially degrade the caloric response of the host alloy
